$comment: The pro registry. STRUCTURE IS TRACKED; KEYS NEVER ARE.
Every key lives in an environment variable named by `key_env`, sourced from a
gitignored .env.local (developer) or a per-repository GitHub secret (CI).
See PRO.md for the inventory this was built from, and part 8's safety rules.
Masteriyo and Lemon Squeezy are deliberately absent: no Lemon Squeezy product
was found in ThemeGrill's catalogue during the inventory, and Masteriyo was
excluded from scope. Adding either is a new entry here plus, for a new
contentgate-pro is absent for a different and more interesting reason: it has
NO licence layer. There is no Freemius, no EDD, no ThemeGrill SDK and no key.
constant the pro build hardcodes to true at contentgate.php:30 — the pro repo
is a repo-sync'd superset of the free one, shipped as one plugin. A row here
would have to name that as its pro_check, and a pro_check that is true by
construction passes invariant 8b without a licence ever resolving, which is
the precise failure 8b exists to prevent. Until the product grows a real
licence layer it belongs on the FREE caller (qa-suite.yml), where `pro`
features are just features and nothing claims to have verified a licence.

colormag-pro.entry_point: FS_ThemeGrill::init() — functions.php:420, wrapping fs_dynamic_init() at functions.php:372
colormag-pro.notes: Standalone pro theme, NOT a child theme and NOT a companion plugin. Replaces the free colormag; the two must never be active at once. Freemius slug is `colormag` with premium_slug `colormag-pro`.

zakra-pro.notes: Companion PLUGIN extending the free Zakra THEME — so the free theme must be mounted and active as well. Belongs to a Freemius bundle (4562); a bundle key is rejected by the product-specific activation path.

user-registration-pro.notes: The store resolves the product from the key alone — no item_id is sent, confirmed at class-ur-plugin-updater-api.php:101-107. `option_status` holds the WHOLE decoded activate response object, not a status string; the licence is valid when its ->license === 'valid'. UR_PRO_ACTIVE is only 'the pro plugin is installed' and says nothing about the licence — do not use it as a pro gate.

everest-forms-pro.notes: Completed 2026-09-08 from the pro plugin checked out at wp-content/plugins/everest-forms-pro (EFP_VERSION 1.9.21), which is what the previous INCOMPLETE note was waiting for. Evidence, all in the pro repo: store_url + api_path come from EVF_Updater_Key_API::$endpoint = 'https://wpeverest.com/edd-sl-api/?' at includes/updater/class-evf-updater-key-api.php:16 — the same host and path as user-registration-pro, as that row predicted (same vendor). option_status is $this->plugin_slug . '_license_active' at class-evf-plugin-updater.php:579, and plugin_slug is basename(plugin_file, '.php') at :29, i.e. 'everest-forms-pro'. Like UR, it stores the WHOLE decoded activate response object, not a status string — the licence is valid when its ->success is true and ->license === 'valid'. item_id stays null: activate() sends only license, url and edd_action (class-evf-updater-key-api.php:79-85), so the store resolves the product from the key alone. The pro gate is unchanged and lives in the FREE plugin: evf_get_license_plan() at includes/evf-core-functions.php:1625 reads get_option('everest-forms-pro_license_key') and requires is_plugin_active('everest-forms-pro/everest-forms-pro.php'). Note its first branch: under REST_REQUEST, DOING_CRON or DOING_AJAX it returns get_option('evf_saved_license_plan', 'personal') and never consults the key at all, so an AJAX-context probe can report a plan on an unlicensed site.

magazine-blocks-pro.entry_point: magazine_blocks_pro_freemius() — magazine-blocks-pro.php:132, wrapping fs_dynamic_init() at :142; called from magazine_blocks_pro_plugin_load(), hooked on plugins_loaded at :208
magazine-blocks-pro.notes: The accessor is a plain global FUNCTION, not a `Class::method` pair like ColorMag's `FS_ThemeGrill::freemius()`. That is a FOURTH expression shape and both mu-plugins had to learn it (tgqa-license.php and tgqa-probe.php); before that, this row's pro_check fell through to 'no recognised pro_check expression' and the gate reported unevaluable, which pro-suite.yml passes with a warning — a @pro run that never checked its licence. The function can also return FALSE (it catches Freemius_Exception and caches false in a global), so the is_object() guard is load-bearing, not defensive habit. Freemius arrives through COMPOSER (`freemius/wordpress-sdk: ^2.11`, locked at 2.12.1), not vendored in-tree like blockart-blocks-pro and not a submodule like colormag-pro — so `composer install` in the pro checkout is a hard prerequisite: magazine-blocks-pro.php:33 requires vendor/autoload.php unconditionally and the plugin fatals without it. Booting this product ALONE is impossible: the header declares `Requires Plugins: magazine-blocks`, so WordPress refuses to activate it and a free-caller boot dies on the activation step — it must go through pro-suite.yml, which checks the free plugin out alongside. One thing a green @pro run does NOT prove: the plugin is `is_premium_only`, so every pro block, REST route and dashboard screen ships unconditionally and the product never consults its own gate to restrict a feature. The single can_use_premium_code() call in the product is at includes/ScriptStyle.php:130 and only decides whether to render the Freemius licence-management UI. pro_check therefore reports faithfully whether the LICENCE RESOLVED — which is what invariant 8b asks of it — and says nothing about whether the features are gated behind it.

blockart-blocks-pro.entry_point: blockart_pro_freemius() — blockart-pro.php:132, wrapping fs_dynamic_init() at :142; called from blockart_pro_plugin_load(), hooked on plugins_loaded at :208
blockart-blocks-pro.notes: Structurally identical to magazine-blocks-pro — same authors, same Freemius shape, same `is_premium_only` caveat about what a green @pro run proves (the sole can_use_premium_code() call is includes/ScriptStyle.php:128, building the licence UI). Three differences worth having written down. First, NOTHING here is named `blockart-blocks-pro` except the repository: the entry file is `blockart-pro.php`, the text domain is `blockart-pro`, and the Freemius slug is `blockart-blocks-pro`. The directory name is what identifies it, which is why boot-wp.mjs discovers the entry file by reading plugin headers instead of deriving `<slug>/<slug>.php` — that derivation would silently fail to activate this one. Second, the Freemius SDK is VENDORED IN-TREE at freemius/ (tracked files, required from blockart-pro.php:139), not pulled by Composer, so the SDK survives a missing `composer install` — but the plugin's own PSR-4 autoloader does not, so composer install is still required. Third, the free plugin's slug is `blockart-blocks` (its Text Domain) while its entry file is `blockart.php`; pro declares `Requires Plugins: blockart-blocks`, so like magazine-blocks-pro it cannot be booted alone.

allcoach-pro.notes: Third provider: the ThemeGrill SDK, driven by scripts/lib/license/themegrill-sdk.mjs. Deliberately NOT `edd`: the SDK posts JSON {license_key, item_id, site_url} to store_url+api_path+<action> (https://api.themegrill.com/licenses/activate) with the action in the PATH, whereas edd.mjs form-posts {edd_action, license, url} to {store}/edd-sl-api/ — the EDD adapter would produce a well-formed request this store does not understand and a false "licence not active". activate/deactivate wrap their payload in a `data` key; `check` returns it flat (Licenser.php:255-260). `option_status` holds a status STRING and the response object goes to `option_data` — the opposite of user-registration-pro, whose option_status holds the whole object. Licensed iff that string is exactly 'valid': the store also returns license="active" with error="site_inactive" for a good key never activated on this site, and that must NOT open the gate. Replacement plugin sharing the text domain `allcoach` with the free plugin, so the DIRECTORY name identifies it; the two must never be active at once (WordPress does not enforce this). Usage tracking is routed under the base slug `allcoach` because api.themegrill.com/tracking/log rejects `allcoach-pro` with a 400 (src/SDK.php:20-32).

spacious-pro.entry_point: FS_ThemeGrill::init() — functions.php:362, wrapping fs_dynamic_init() at functions.php:317
spacious-pro.notes: Same shape as colormag-pro: a standalone pro THEME replacing the free spacious, never active alongside it; Freemius slug `spacious` with premium_slug `spacious-pro`; the SDK is a git submodule at freemius/, so checkout needs `submodules: recursive` or FS_ThemeGrill::init() silently returns null. `is_premium_only`, and the only can_use_premium_code() call outside the SDK is inc/freemius-migration.php, so like the block plugins a green @pro run proves the licence RESOLVED, not that any feature is gated behind it.
